propositions: A git merge abort triggered by local changes to tracked files ('Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge') leaves reconverge unable to advance and strands local ticket commits off origin
Tracked file deletions in the worktree (staged or unstaged) and tracked file modifications must be recovered by restoring from HEAD and/or quarantining local bytes before retry

The recovery mechanism detects the merge-abort signature, parses named paths from git output, classifies each path by porcelain status (D for deletion, M for modification), restores deletions via git checkout, quarantines modified content before restoring, and retries the merge once
A genuine merge conflict (both sides commit different content to the same file) preserves today's abort-only behavior without self-healing
The recovery seam reuses the parsing and quarantine pattern established in change 1757 for untracked-file overwrites, extending one proven mechanism rather than adding a second
